title: Cold outbound sequences from a lead list
prompt:
Brackenfold is starting cold outbound email. Turn the supplied lead list into ready-to-load sequences, following the supplied outbound standard exactly and using only the supplied product facts.

Deliver three files in your reply. Put each one under a line with its file name, as CSV with exactly the header shown: one row per item, no totals row, and nothing inside the file but its rows. If a value contains a comma, put the value in double quotes. A body is one line: never put a line break inside it, and write " / " between its paragraphs.

### excluded.csv
lead_id,reason
Every lead the standard excludes, with the reason code from Step 1.

### assignments.csv
lead_id,segment,country_group
Every lead that is not excluded, with its segment code from Step 2 and its country group code from Step 3.

### sequences.csv
segment,country_group,step,send_day,subject,body
One row per email: every step of the sequence of each segment and country group that has at least one assigned lead. `step` is the step number and `send_day` the day from Step 4. Write merge fields as {{name}}; they are filled when the emails are sent.

Every lead in leads.csv appears exactly once, in excluded.csv or in assignments.csv, and no lead_id appears that is not in leads.csv.

End your reply with this answer block, one line per answer: the label, a colon and the number alone.

A1: <number of leads excluded>
A2: <number of leads assigned>
A3: <emails the first full run sends: for each assigned lead, the number of steps in its sequence, added up>

This is a plan for review. Send nothing, load nothing into any tool and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: All three files (excluded.csv, assignments.csv, sequences.csv) are in the reply, each under a line with its file name.

Every one of the list's 200 leads appears exactly once across excluded.csv and assignments.csv, and no lead_id appears that is not in the list. Full credit for none missing, repeated or invented; zero credit at 10 or more.
The reply ends with the answer block and all 3 labeled answers A1-A3 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states how many leads the standard excludes. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 5 or more off.
A2 states how many leads the standard assigns to a sequence. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 10 or more off.

A3 states how many emails the first full run sends: every assigned lead times the steps of its own sequence, the restricted group's shorter sequences included. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 25 or more off.

skill_adherence.check: The leads excluded are exactly the ones Step 1 excludes: none emailed that should be excluded, none excluded that should be emailed. Full credit for no difference; zero credit at 10 or more.
Every excluded lead carries the code of the first Step 1 reason that applies to it. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 5 or more.
Every assigned lead is in the segment Step 2 gives it. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 10 or more.
Every assigned lead is in the country group Step 3 gives it. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 8 or more.

sequences.csv has exactly one row for every step of every sequence Step 4 calls for (the restricted group's two steps only, and no sequence for a segment and country group with no assigned lead). Full credit for none missing, repeated or extra; zero credit at 3 or more.
Every step is sent on the day Step 4 gives it, the restricted group's minimum gap applied. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 3 or more.

best_practices.check: Every email has a subject of at most 45 characters as written that does not start with Re:, Fwd: or Fw:. Full credit for none missing, over or faked as a reply; zero credit at 3 or more.
No two emails of the programme share a subject, case, spacing, punctuation and merge fields aside. Full credit for none repeated or missing; zero credit at 3 or more.
Every email has a body of at most 110 words. Full credit for none missing or over; zero credit at 3 or more.
Every body ends with the standard's unsubscribe sentence followed by the postal address, word for word. Full credit for none missing or out of place; zero credit at 3 or more.

Every restricted email carries the legitimate-interest sentence and every canada email the Canadian line, word for word, and no other email carries either. Full credit for none missing or misplaced; zero credit at 4 or more.
No subject or body uses a phrase the standard forbids. Full credit for none; zero credit at 3 or more.
Every merge field is one the standard allows ({{first_name}}, {{company}}, {{industry}}). Full credit for none other; zero credit at 3 or more.

No email uses a merge field that some lead of its sequence has no value for, and every body opens with the greeting Step 6 gives its sequence (Hi {{first_name}}, or Hi there,). Full credit for none wrong; zero credit at 3 or more.
Every email cites exactly one proof point, and every figure in its subject and body is one the product facts state, the postal address aside. Full credit for none wrong; zero credit at 3 or more.

Judge the sequences.csv rows only. The emails are written for their segment and step: across segments they differ in substance (the problem they open with, the angle, the ask), and within a sequence each step brings something the one before did not, not one email with a word swapped. The same segment and step may share copy across country groups. It fails if most rows are the same template, or if sequences.csv is missing.
